interactions.hypothesis: Playoff odds x contract status: sellers with expiring contracts are most likely traded, so standing and contract status interact for trade probability.
Rule calendar x report timing: option/40-man deadlines concentrate moves on specific dates, so hazards should be date-aware and reports tighten the window.
Report credibility x price reaction: price changes after reports measure their credibility and the rules define whether they count.

A seller with an expiring contract in the final weeks before the deadline has a trade hazard that is the product of team status (seller), player contract (expiring, tradable) and calendar proximity, so none of these alone predicts a trade; each multiplies the daily hazard.

The completion probability given a report depends on wording and source, and on whether the rules count only the official announcement; a credible 'pending physical' report implies high probability of completion within days but not certainty. The official-versus-report distinction is an assumption about settlement until the full rules are read.

Payroll headroom acts as a threshold: teams near the tax line are very unlikely to add salary beyond it, so a free-agent signing probability for that team is near zero until headroom exceeds the contract's annual value; contract structure shifts the effective threshold.

Managers are fired in-season mainly when the team is out of contention, and in the offseason after the season ends; the hazard regime switches at the end of the season, and the next-manager market depends on a vacancy created in the first regime or second.
Injury-driven call-ups and IL moves are constrained by roster and option rules, so the number of available call-up slots and the date relative to roster expansions changes the hazard in steps.

During a lockout the signing hazard is zero and the destination choice cannot resolve; after an agreement the pent-up signings arrive in a rush on compressed calendar anchors, so the probability a named destination wins before March 25 2027 equals P(lockout ends in time) times the post-deal destination share.

On deadline day many agreements are reported in the final hour, and the trade market counts only those officially processed before the date; a credible report of an agreed deal minutes before the deadline converts to Yes only if processing lands in time, and players with no-trade or 10-and-5 rights add a consent step that can push completion past the cutoff.

transactions.label: Transactions, coaching and personnel events
transactions.mechanism: Transactions follow institutional calendars and team incentives: standing (buyer vs seller), contract status, roster-rule constraints and front-office behaviour, with beat-writer reports preceding many official moves. The probability is a hazard over the contract window, estimated from reference classes and updated by reports and standings, with the resolution defined by official announcement.
transactions.target: Whether a trade, signing, call-up, extension or manager/coach change occurs by a given date.

interactions.hypothesis: Production rank x team success: voters weigh WAR with team record, so candidates on playoff teams gain relative to equal production on non-playoff teams.
Ballot timing x injuries: votes cast before the postseason make late-season results irrelevant, so injuries after the ballot deadline should not move the probability.

awards_mkt.mechanism: Voters choose from visible production and team narrative at a fixed time and with a specific ballot structure; the best model is a historical voter-behaviour model using WAR, counting stats and team success, updated by finalist announcements. Late-season results matter less if ballots are cast before the postseason.
awards_mkt.target: Winner or finalist of a league award (MVP, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year, Manager of the Year, Gold Glove), as announced by the award body.

interactions.hypothesis: Precipitation timing x roof status: the same forecast produces a delay only if the roof is open; roof state must gate the weather risk.
Definition of delay x time window: contracts counting only start delays are driven by pre-first-pitch weather while in-game delay contracts add game-length exposure.

delay.mechanism: Delay probability is a weather-timing problem: precipitation (or lightning) likelihood and intensity near first pitch relative to the roof status, and the decision behaviour of umpire crew and teams. It is largely independent of team quality; the information value is in forecast updates and in historical delay behaviour by park.
delay.target: Whether a game is delayed (start delayed or play stopped for weather), postponed or suspended, per the contract definition.

inputs.why: Tied-after-nine rate by total/spread bucket.
Distribution shape drives P(tie).
Strong starters lower totals and raise tie chance.
Late scoring quality: relief pitchers' quality sets run prevention after the starter exits, determining full-game total and winner.
Low-scoring parks tie more: park dimensions, altitude and surface change run, HR and hit probabilities for both teams, and by batter handedness.
Weather shifts run scoring: temperature, air density and wind change ball flight, so fly-ball outcomes (HR, doubles) vary with conditions.
Offence quality sets run levels.
Rule for ghost runner: from the tenth inning each half-inning starts with a runner on second (ghost runner), making extra innings short and shifting expectation of the winner.

Wording for extras: the settlement wording defines which events count (overtime, extra innings, shootout goals, delayed games, DNPs) and therefore changes the true probability of the same real-world sport.

interactions.hypothesis: Low total x small spread: ties peak when both teams are expected to score little and are evenly matched, so the tie probability is a function of total and spread jointly.
Late-inning run scoring determines whether a tie at 9 persists; bullpen quality and manager decisions in innings 7-9 interact with starter exit.

extras.mechanism: Extra innings require a tie after nine innings; the probability is the probability that the two teams' run totals are equal, which is higher in low-scoring, close-spread games. The ghost-runner rule shortens extra innings but does not affect the event of reaching extras. Estimation requires a calibrated run distribution (with overdispersion and team correlation) and the contract's inclusion rule.
extras.target: Whether the game goes to extra innings (tied after nine), and related game-length outcomes.

Top-of-order quality vs starter.

interactions.hypothesis: Top-of-order OBP x starter command: the chance of a walk or hit by the first three batters scales with their OBP and the starter's zone rate, so the product (and the two-half-inning union) determines the event probability.
Starter first-trip profile x platoon: lefty-heavy top order against a righty with weak changeup raises first-inning scoring, so platoon should be applied at the top-three level.

first_inning_mkt.mechanism: The first inning is the top three batters of each lineup against fresh starters, so the run probability is a function of those six hitters' on-base and power against the starting pitchers' first-trip profile, with park and weather scaling. The event is a union over two half-innings, each with roughly a modest probability, so the outcome is sensitive to the top-of-order quality and to the starter's early command; small samples make first-inning historical splits unreliable.
first_inning_mkt.target: Whether a run is scored in the first inning (by either team or by a specific team), and first-inning run counts.

interactions.hypothesis: Starter quality only matters for the innings he pitches, so starter edge should be weighted by expected batters faced and the quality gap to the bullpen that replaces him.
Lineup handedness against starter handedness: a platoon-weak confirmed lineup lowers team strength more than season-level wRC+ suggests, so team offence should be lineup-by-hand specific.
Wind and park interact: wind-out adds more runs in HR-friendly parks and for fly-ball pitchers, so the effect should be multiplied with park HR factor and pitcher fly-ball rate.

game_side.mechanism: Win probability follows from the expected run difference: starter run prevention for the innings he works, bullpen quality for the rest, lineup quality against the specific starter's handedness and arsenal, and park/weather/umpire scaling of both offences. Home field adds a small edge. Because late information (confirmed lineups, scratched starter, weather) moves the line, the model's value comes from timely incorporation and from regressing luck-heavy team results; margin and spread contracts additionally need the run-difference distribution including extra-innings tie breaking.
game_side.target: Which team wins the game (and by how many runs for spread/margin contracts), settled after the final out including extra innings unless the wording says otherwise.

interactions.hypothesis: Wind, temperature and park multiply: the same wind adds more in a HR-friendly park and in hot, thin air, so the weather effect must be estimated with park interaction terms.

Starter quality x expected innings x bullpen quality: run total is a mixture of starter-run-rate and bullpen-run-rate by innings, so the starter's hook probability interacts with the bullpen's quality.
Umpire zone x pitcher type: a large zone lowers totals more for hitters' counts and for command pitchers than for high-walk pitchers, so the umpire effect depends on pitcher walk profile.

game_total.mechanism: Expected runs are the sum over plate appearances of per-PA run value, determined by starter quality for the early innings, bullpen quality for the late innings, the lineups' quality by handedness, park and weather (air density, wind), and the umpire's zone. Run distributions are overdispersed and clustered by inning, so threshold prices depend on dispersion and not just the mean; late-breaking information (confirmed lineups, wind, roof status, scratched starters) is the main source of mispricing.
game_total.target: Total runs (or one team's runs) in the game, with the contract defining whether extra-innings runs count and how shortened games settle.

True-talent rate for hitters: a hitter's quality per plate appearance (on-base skill, power, contact quality) determines hits, bases, runs and RBIs.
True-talent for pitchers' stats.

Opportunity (PA) projection: pA count is the volume multiplier for hits, TB, HR, RBI and runs, and depends on the lineup slot, the team's run environment and the opposing pitcher.

Which stat source and date: the settlement wording defines which events count (overtime, extra innings, shootout goals, delayed games, DNPs) and therefore changes the true probability of the same real-world sport.

interactions.hypothesis: Rate x opportunity: the final total is current total plus per-game rate times games played, so injury probability interacts with talent for leaders.
Qualification rules x rate stats: borderline players may qualify only by PA accrual, so playing time interacts with batting title markets.

Rate stats require qualification; races depend on the top-tail distribution of contenders and on injuries. Because early-season leaders are driven by luck, rate regression to talent is the main lever.
leaders.target: Season leaders or cumulative totals (HR, RBI, hits, batting average, strikeouts, saves, ERA) as of the end of the regular season or a defined date.

lineup_role.mechanism: Participation is determined by manager decisions (rest days, platoon matchups), injury status and late scratches, and the lineup card posted a few hours before the game; before the card, probability is a function of rest-day patterns and matchup, after the card it is nearly certain except for in-game substitutions. The key is timing and the exact definition of 'play'.
lineup_role.target: Whether a player plays, starts or enters the game (participation markets), per the contract's definition.

interactions.hypothesis: Crew vocabulary x event triggers: the probability of a word equals baseline crew rate plus a trigger bump when the relevant event occurs, so event likelihood should be modelled separately.
Airtime length: delays and extra innings lengthen the broadcast, raising the chance of any word, so game-length uncertainty interacts with word rate.

mentions.mechanism: Mentions depend on the announcers' vocabulary and on game events that trigger topics (milestones, pitching changes, weather), so the best-supported hypotheses concern crew habits, broadcast length and event likelihood; sports performance statistics have little direct predictive role. interactions.hypothesis: Base rate x time remaining: the hazard concentrates around known dates, so base rates must be time-conditioned by the market window.
News timing x resolution source: reports precede official announcements; the wording defines whether a report counts, so price reaction should be read against the rules.

off_field.mechanism: These markets depend on organisational decisions and external events rather than on-field performance. There is no strong statistical structure; value, if any, comes from reference-class frequencies, calendar constraints and timestamped news relative to the resolution wording. Many are effectively novelty markets with weak predictability from baseball data.

interactions.hypothesis: Starter exit before the fifth is a mixture: P(early exit) x bullpen quality vs P(full five) x starter quality, so leash and bullpen state interact with starter quality in F5.

F5 tie probability is high enough that spread/winner contracts differ by tie rule; the rules interact with run-distribution shape.

period.mechanism: F5 isolates starters: run scoring is determined by the starters' quality over their first two trips through the order, the lineups' strength against them, park and weather, with the bullpen entering only when the starter is pulled early. Starter exit probability before the fifth is the major structural uncertainty and ties are possible, so rules matter (push vs loss).

Batters faced multiplier: batters faced is the volume multiplier for every pitcher counting stat (strikeouts, outs, hits, walks, earned runs) and sets how much bullpen exposure the game has.
Confirmed lineup patience: who bats and in what order determines the actual hitters a pitcher faces and the plate appearances each hitter gets.
Zone size changes ball/strike calls.
Receiving adds borderline strikes.
Patient lineups draw more walks.
Fatigue/injury effects on command.

Park and weather effects on grip/ball.
Weather effects on command: temperature, air density and wind change ball flight, so fly-ball outcomes (HR, doubles) vary with conditions.
Walk rungs consistency: rungs of a threshold ladder (e.g.

interactions.hypothesis: Pitcher zone rate x lineup chase rate: patient lineups walk more against pitchers who miss the zone, but chase-prone lineups reduce walks even against wild pitchers, so command and discipline interact.
Umpire zone x framing: small-zone umpires and weak framers raise walks, so the effect is larger for pitchers who rely on edge pitches.

pitcher_bb.mechanism: Walks = batters faced x per-PA BB probability, which combines the pitcher's command (zone rate, first-pitch strikes) with the lineup's patience and chase rates, modified by umpire zone and catcher framing. Counts are low and overdispersed, with intentional walks adding rare cases; workload and the hook matter, and walk-prone starters also tend to be pulled early.
pitcher_bb.target: Walks allowed by the starting pitcher in the game (threshold ladder).

inputs.why: Skill-based run-prevention estimate (SIERA/xFIP).
Batters faced determine exposure.
Early hook caps accumulating runs.
Lineup quality against the pitcher's handedness.
Confirmed lineup replaces probable.

HR risk drives earned runs: pitchers who allow fly balls and hard contact give up more home runs, and the hitter-pitcher combination determines the single-game probability.

Strand and BABIP luck: observed ER overstate or understate true run prevention; ER projections should use expected rates from K, BB, HR and contact quality.

pitcher_er.mechanism: Earned runs result from baserunners (hits, walks, HBP) and their conversion into runs given HR, sequencing and the bullpen's handling of inherited runners; they depend on batters faced (so on the hook) and per-PA run value. Luck components (BABIP, LOB%, HR/FB) are large, so skill-based estimators and regression matter; the right tail is driven by HR and by blow-up innings that also trigger early hooks.
pitcher_er.target: Earned runs allowed by the starting pitcher in the game (threshold ladder).

Defence x ground-ball rate: infield defence quality matters more for ground-ball pitchers, so GB% interacts with team defence for hit probability.

pitcher_hits.mechanism: Hits allowed = balls in play x hit probability (a function of contact quality, defence, park and BABIP) plus home runs; K and BB rates determine how many batters put the ball in play. Variance is high and BABIP is mostly noise beyond contact quality, so expected-BABIP models and defence behind the pitcher are central; workload (batters faced) scales the total.

interactions.hypothesis: PA count x per-PA probability: a bottom-order hitter with equal skill gets fewer PAs; expected hits thus depend jointly on slot and team total.
Pitch-type matchup x platoon: a hitter's weakness to breaking balls matters more against same-handed breaking-ball-heavy starters, so platoon and pitch-mix effects should be modelled jointly.
BABIP luck x contact quality: recent hit totals overstate skill when xBA lags, so xBA-based projections should replace observed hits.

player_hit.mechanism: Each count is the sum over the hitter's plate appearances of per-PA outcome probabilities, so expected value = expected PA (lineup slot, team scoring, substitution risk) x per-PA rates (contact quality, K/BB, platoon, pitch-type matchup, park, weather, defence) with the opposing starter's quality for the first two or three PAs and the bullpen for the rest. RBI, runs and SB additionally depend on teammates' on-base and the situation, making them more variable and less skill-pure.
player_hit.target: Hitter counting outcomes in a game: hits, total bases, RBIs, runs or stolen bases (threshold ladders), requiring the player to appear per the wording.

interactions.hypothesis: Hitter pull-air x park pull-side HR factor x wind: HR probability depends on whether the hitter's fly balls go to the park's short side with wind, so these three need joint modelling.
Barrel rate x pitcher HR vulnerability: pitchers who throw center-cut fastballs raise HR chance most for hitters with high fastball barrel rates, so matchup beats aggregate rates.
PA count x per-PA HR: expected HR scales with plate appearances, so confirmed batting slot and team total directly shift the probability.

player_hr.mechanism: HR is a rare per-PA event whose probability is the hitter's HR rate (barrels, pull-air, FB%) modified by the pitcher's HR vulnerability, platoon, park HR factor by handedness and weather (wind, temperature), multiplied across expected PAs and hits against starter and bullpen. Variance is intrinsic; HR/FB luck regresses. Small multiplicative shifts in environment matter because of the low base probability.

interactions.hypothesis: Pitch mix x lineup whiff by pitch: the strikeout rate is the usage-weighted sum of pitcher whiff and lineup whiff for each pitch type, not the product of aggregate K% rates.

Times-through-order x hook: the K rate decays by trip while the probability of reaching the third trip depends on pitch count and leash, so expected K is a sum over trips weighted by survival probabilities.

Umpire zone x called-strike rate: a larger zone helps pitchers who live on the edges (high called-strike rate), a smaller zone helps hitters, so the umpire effect should be scaled by the pitcher's edge-pitch share and catcher framing.
Pitch cap x efficiency x patience: outs scale with pitch cap divided by pitches per PA, which depends on the opposing lineup's patience, so the cap and lineup patience interact for outs markets.

player_pitch.mechanism: Strikeouts = batters faced x per-PA K probability and outs = batters faced x (1 - on-base events), so the outcome is workload times rate. Workload (batters faced) is limited by the pitch cap divided by pitches per PA and by performance-based hooks (the manager's leash, times-through-order, score), while the per-PA K probability combines the pitcher's pitch-level whiff ability with the confirmed lineup's whiff and K tendencies by handedness, modulated by the umpire's zone, catcher framing and park, and diminishing across the order. Realized pitch count is not known pregame; only its distribution is.
player_pitch.target: Starting pitcher counting stats: strikeouts or outs recorded in the game (threshold ladder), requiring the pitcher to start per the wording.

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook / exchange reference prices with timestamps
m.external_lines.measurement: Capture timestamped lines per book; de-vig (power or Shin method) per market; map to the Kalshi contract's rule (regulation vs full game, push handling); compute Kalshi minus consensus and closing-line value relative to the latest pregame consensus.
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sharp sportsbook and exchange lines are a competing aggregation of information and the standard benchmark for fair probability.
m.external_lines.rationale: Using a de-vigged external line as a feature or benchmark is often a stronger baseline than any public-stats model, and disagreement with Kalshi flags either a stale Kalshi quote or a rule-wording difference. Subtle: books price different settlement terms (e.g. regulation vs including overtime, 'action' rules on postponements) so lines must be mapped to the Kalshi rule before comparison, and the timestamp of the line matters.

m.fees.label: Fee schedule and maker/taker rules in force
m.fees.measurement: Version the fee formula from Kalshi's published fee schedule; compute breakeven probability per price and role; subtract from model edge before any threshold decision.
m.fees.mechanism: Fees reduce realized edge and depend on price level, so the break-even probability differs by rung and by maker/taker role.
m.fees.rationale: Because the fee is price-dependent, a fixed edge in cents is worth less near 50 than at the tails or vice versa depending on schedule; a model signal must clear fee-adjusted breakeven, not raw midpoint difference. Subtle: fee schedules change over time and by market type, so the version in force at trade time must be used.

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder (monotonicity, implied distribution)
m.ladder_structure.measurement: For each event/player collect all live rungs at one timestamp; check P(k) non-increasing; fit a discrete distribution (Poisson, negative binomial, or free-form isotonic) to mid prices; compare implied mean/variance and per-rung residual to the model; track which rungs the market lags when news arrives.
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: Rungs of a threshold ladder (e.g. 4+, 5+, 6+) must imply one coherent count distribution; deviations expose stale or mispriced rungs and reveal the market's implied mean and variance.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Ladders for the same player/game are strongly correlated, so edges on adjacent rungs are not independent bets and exposure must be sized per ladder. Subtle: because each rung is a survival probability P(X>=k), monotone non-increasing is a hard constraint, and fitting a Poisson/negative-binomial to the rungs gives an implied mean that can be compared to a model mean on a like-for-like basis.

m.orderbook_depth.label: Order-book depth and spread
m.orderbook_depth.measurement: Snapshot the book (top-N levels both sides) at fixed intervals before start; compute spread, depth within 2 cents of mid, imbalance. Compare model edge to half-spread plus fee to get executable edge.
m.orderbook_depth.mechanism: Depth and spread determine whether a modelled edge can be executed and how much the quoted price reflects informed versus noise flow.
m.orderbook_depth.rationale: Wide spreads and thin depth on MLB prop and long-tail rungs mean the midpoint is a noisy probability estimate and the edge after crossing the spread may be negative. Subtle: historical depth is only available if captured live, so the pregame view is whatever was snapshotted; reconstructing it from trades is approximate.

mlb.abs_challenge_regime.label: ABS challenge-system zone regime (2026+): effective zone, challenge availability and success, catcher/batter challenge skill
mlb.abs_challenge_regime.measurement: Using 2026+ pitch-level data with challenge events, per battery (pitcher-catcher) and batter: (a) edge_cs = share of pitches within 1.5 inches of the rulebook zone edge that end as called strikes after any overturn; (b) challenge_rate = challenges per 100 edge pitches taken and overturn_rate = overturned/challenges, each shrunk to the league rate with k = 30 challenges; (c) league_shift = league edge_cs 2026-to-date minus 2025 edge_cs at matched counts. Pre-2026 umpire and framing effects are rescaled by r = SD across umpires of edge_cs in 2026 divided by the same SD in 2025, with r = 1 until 100 edge pitches per umpire exist and r regressed to 1 with k = 500 edge pitches. Output: change in edge-pitch called-strike probability and in K% and BB% per PA (probability points, using the league K/BB elasticity to edge_cs fitted 2021-2025). As-of: games completed before the target first pitch.
mlb.abs_challenge_regime.mechanism: With automated ball-strike challenges, a borderline pitch can be overturned to the true zone, so called-strike probability on edge pitches, framing value and umpire zone effects shrink toward the robotic zone and challenge skill matters.

mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.label: Joint distribution of award outcomes for combination markets
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.measurement: For awards A and B, take marginals P(A), P(B) from mlb.award_vote_rank_model (never from prices). Define relation group g in {same team, same league different team, different league} for the two candidate outcomes. From 1996-2025 winners compute lift_g = [n_AB,g / n_g] / [P_hist(A) * P_hist(B)] where n_AB,g counts seasons both events in group g happened and n_g counts seasons the pair was possible; shrink lift_shrunk = 1 + (lift_g - 1) * n_g / (n_g + 10). Then P(A and B) = min(P(A), P(B), P(A) * P(B) * lift_shrunk). Output P(A and B) and the ratio to the product. As-of: after finalists are announced, using only winners before the snapshot.
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.mechanism: A combination market pays only if several awards go to specified outcomes, whose probabilities are correlated through shared player performance and team narrative.
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.rationale: KXMLBAWARDCOMBO needs P(A and B), not the product: an MVP and Cy Young from the same team are positively dependent via team success, while two MVPs in different leagues are nearly independent; the electorates also differ.

Expected TB per PA = P(BIP | PA) * [P(1B) + 2*P(2B) + 3*P(3B) + 4*P(HR)] with P(BIP | PA) = 1 - K% - BB% - HBP% (HR counted inside BIP); strikeouts and walks contribute 0. Units: bases per PA. Convert to expected intentional-plus-unintentional walk-rate shift using a regression of BB% on protection with first-base-open flag over 2021-2025 (shrunk by hitter with k = 200 PA). Output: change in per-PA walk probability and in the P(runner goes) at first base. As-of: lineup post.
mlb.batting_behind_protection.mechanism: Pitchers and managers decide whether to pitch to or around a hitter, and whether to hold or send a runner, based on who follows; a weak hitter on deck raises walks and intentional walks for the current hitter and lowers his RBI chances.
mlb.batting_behind_protection.rationale: RBI conversion and steal attempts both depend on the batter behind: with first base open a dangerous on-deck hitter lowers the walk rate, while a weak one invites intentional walks that remove RBI chances. This is stated only in interactions today and has no measurable input; it also changes the green light for a runner on first.

mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.label: Bonus-pool and slot-value structure: assigned slot values per pick, club pool size, overage tax and forfeiture thresholds, and incentives for underslot top picks
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.measurement: Per club and draft year (pool system from 2012): pool_total = sum of official slot values of the club's picks in rounds 1-10 as published before the draft, n_top75 = picks in slots 1-75, first_pick_share = first-pick slot value / pool_total. Historical discount for picks in slots 1-10 = (signed bonus - slot value) / slot value. underslot_score_c = share of the club's slot 1-10 picks signed below slot over the last 8 drafts, shrunk to the league share with k = 4 picks, a value in [0,1]. Record the CBA overage tax and pick-forfeiture tiers as constants and verify against the CBA text. Use only signings completed before the snapshot; the current class's bonuses are excluded. As-of: pool release and signings to date.
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.mechanism: Clubs maximise total draft value under a hard-ish bonus pool, so taking a cheaper player at a high slot frees money for later picks.
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.rationale: Exceeding the pool by up to 5% costs a 75% tax and larger overages cost future first-round picks, so pools act as a budget constraint. Clubs with several early picks or a deep later class have strong incentives to sign the slot-5 pick below value, which favours college seniors and players with low leverage over the consensus talent.

mlb.bottom_ninth_truncation.label: Probability the home team's bottom of the ninth is skipped (home lead after 8.5) and its run-total effect
mlb.bottom_ninth_truncation.measurement: Take P(home skips bottom 9) = P(home leads after the top of the 9th) from mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher (not recomputed). Combined-total truncation loss = P(skip) * mu9, mu9 = the home team's expected runs in a full bottom-9 half inning (about 0.5, estimated from half-inning data 2015-2025 with team shrinkage k = 100 half-innings). Walk-off truncation: when the home team trails by d or is tied entering the bottom 9th or later, the half ends when it takes the lead, so its expected runs = E[min(runs, d+1)] with the exception that a home run counts every run on the play, computed from a base-out Markov chain with the team's PA outcome rates. Apply the loss to the home team total and the combined total, not to the visitor total. Output expected truncation in runs for home total, visitor total and combined total. As-of: lineup post.
mlb.bottom_ninth_truncation.mechanism: A home team ahead after the top of the ninth does not bat, so its runs and the game total are truncated relative to nine full innings.
mlb.bottom_ninth_truncation.rationale: A total of 8.5 is often priced as if both teams bat nine innings; in games where the home team is ahead the home runs stop early, shifting probability toward under, and the truncation is correlated with favorite status and low total.

mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.label: Calendar hazard function by transaction type (trade, free-agent signing, extension, manager hire)
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.measurement: From 2010-2025 MLB transactions, for each type define the eligible stock on day d: trades = 40-man players not on a long-term IL; FA signings = unsigned free agents; extensions = players with 1-2 years of control left; manager hires = open vacancies. Daily hazard h(d) = events on d / eligible stock at d. Fit a Poisson log-linear model h(d) = exp(a_type + sum_k b_k * anchor_k(d) + season trend) with anchors (trade deadline +-7 days, winter meetings week, non-tender day, spring training start, opening day); shrink each b_k toward its pooled across-type value with k = 3 seasons. Lockout days (2021-12-02 to 2022-03-10) are excluded from the fit and set to structural zero for 40-man transactions. Output h(d) for the window dates and survival to the window end. As-of: current eligible stock.
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.mechanism: Hazard of each event type is concentrated on known dates.
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.rationale: Using a flat per-day rate misprices markets that straddle deadlines and meeting dates; for example, a large share of free-agent signings occur in specific off-season windows and trade completions spike near the deadline.

mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.label: Final first-round draft order: which club holds each overall slot 1-10 after lottery, reverse-record fill, CBT pick moves and inserted compensation picks
mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.measurement: Procedure for the draft year: (1) assign picks 1-6 by the published lottery odds for non-playoff clubs; before the lottery output P(club holds slot k) from 10,000 simulations; (2) apply the CBA's lottery-restriction placement for ineligible clubs (verify numeric rule against the CBA text); (3) fill remaining slots by reverse prior-season winning percentage among non-playoff clubs with the official tiebreak; (4) move the highest pick of clubs over the CBT draft-penalty tier back ten places unless it is a top-6 pick (verify tier against the CBA); (5) insert compensation picks for unsigned previous-year first-rounders at original slot + 1 and renumber. Output club_id per overall slot with the official order release timestamp. Every item marked verify must be checked against CBA text before use.
mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.mechanism: An exact-slot contract is a statement about the club holding that slot, so the slot-to-club map must be resolved before any prospect preference applies.
mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.rationale: The lottery fixes picks 1-6 only; slots 7-18 follow reverse record among non-playoff clubs that missed the lottery, a club far over the top luxury-tax threshold has its first pick moved back ten places (outside the top six), and a prior-year unsigned first-rounder yields an inserted compensation pick one slot later, which renumbers every later pick. First-round picks cannot be traded in MLB, so unlike other leagues the map is fixed once these rules run.

mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.label: Sequential draft selection engine: club-specific rank-ordered choice over the remaining pool, giving P(prospect taken at slot k) and P(taken by slot N)
mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.measurement: For slot k held by club c, choice probability over remaining prospects i is multinomial logit with U_ci = -alpha*rank_i + beta_c . x_i + gamma*report_shift_i - delta*risk_i, where rank_i = consensus rank at the as-of date (mean of MLB Pipeline, Baseball America, FanGraphs), x_i = (college, pitcher, underslot-fit) with club coefficients beta_c shrunk to the pooled coefficient with k = 6 picks, report_shift_i from mlb.draft_insider_slot_reports, risk_i = medical and signability flags. Fit alpha, beta, gamma, delta by maximum likelihood on 2012-2025 first rounds, using only pre-draft boards. Simulate the draft sequentially 50,000 times removing selected prospects; output P(prospect at slot k) and P(slot <= m). As-of: board and report snapshot with the final slot-owner map.
mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.mechanism: The draft is a sequence of without-replacement choices: each club's choice depends on who remains, so pick probabilities across prospects and slots are jointly constrained.
mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.rationale: Exact-slot probabilities for one prospect over slots 1..N plus P(not in top N) must sum to one, and across prospects each slot is taken by exactly one player. A rank-ordered (Plackett-Luce) choice model with club-specific utility shifts captures cascades: if two players go earlier than expected, the named player is more likely to fall to a given slot. It is a derived model that consumes the information inputs, so it is listed only as the structural constraint on them.

mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.label: Expected unearned-run share (team errors, passed balls, catcher and infield error rates)
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.measurement: Team factor f_team = u_team/u_league, where u_team = unearned runs per game over the last 2 seasons with half-life 60 games shrunk to league with k = 40 games. Pitcher factor f_p = (pitcher unearned share over 3 seasons shrunk to league with k = 300 BF)/league share. Fielder factor f_def = sum over confirmed fielders of error rate per chance (shrunk to league with k = 400 chances) relative to league, weighted by position error-opportunity shares; catcher factor f_c = (passed balls + wild pitches per 100 innings, shrunk with k = 600 innings)/league. unearned_share = league_share * (f_team * f_p * f_def * f_c)^(1/2) clipped to [0.5, 2] x league_share. Expected ER = expected runs * (1 - unearned_share). Units: fraction of runs. As-of: lineup post.
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.mechanism: Runs after an error or passed ball that extends an inning can be unearned and are not counted.
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.rationale: Earned runs are what the contract pays on; runs can differ. Teams with poor infield defense or a passed-ball-prone catcher have a larger gap, and an error that extends an inning raises the number of batters faced and baserunners without adding earned runs.

mlb.exit_boundary_mass.label: Manager exit-boundary mass: P(removal at outs = 3k | reached) with run-state conditioning
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.measurement: For every start in the last 4 seasons record exit_outs. For the current manager only (reset on a change), estimate the discrete hazard g_j = P(removed with exactly j outs | still pitching when reaching j outs) for j = 3..26 in cells of pitch-count bucket at that moment (<85, 85-100, >100) x run-state bucket (leading, tied or trailing by <=2, trailing by >=3); shrink each cell to the league cell with k = 30 starts. Do not smooth across inning boundaries. The distribution of exit_outs is f(j) = g_j * prod_{i<j} (1 - g_i), and P(outs >= m) = prod_{i<m} (1 - g_i), with the pitch-count bucket at each j set from the pitcher's pitches per out. As-of: games through the previous day.
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.mechanism: Starter removals cluster at inning boundaries and at the start of the third time through, and each manager has a characteristic exit lattice.
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.rationale: Outs ladders sit on multiples of three; if removals are smooth, P(outs>=15) and P(outs>=16) are priced alike, but if the manager lets starters finish innings then 16-17 outs are rare while 15 and 18 carry mass. Existing leash does not carry this discreteness.

mlb.extras_run_contribution.label: Expected runs added by extra innings, by rule regime (regular-season automatic runner vs postseason bases-empty) and contract scope

Use the regime flag from the game type (regular season vs postseason) and set to 0 if rules say regulation only. Units: expected runs. As-of: lineup post and contract text version.
mlb.extras_run_contribution.mechanism: A game tied after nine adds extra half-innings; in the regular season each starts with a runner on second, in the postseason (to my knowledge, unverified for 2026) each starts with bases empty, so the runs added differ by regime; runs there count only if the contract counts them.
mlb.extras_run_contribution.rationale: About one game in ten adds a few runs, which matters for rungs near the median; if the contract excludes extras, then these runs must be removed and shortened-game and walk-off logic differ.

mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.label: Schedule map from start date to games played: games per calendar day, scheduled finish date and make-up capacity
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.measurement: From the published schedule file (version at the snapshot) compute N(d) = league games scheduled on or after date d, and for each club the open dates in [d, last day]. Predicted games G(d) = N(d) + (sum over 30 clubs of recoverable games)/2. Solve d* such that G(d*) = 600 games and also output the date after which fewer than 600 games remain. As-of: schedule version available at the snapshot.
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.mechanism: Games played in a shortened season equals scheduled games on dates after the first game, plus any games the league can add through doubleheaders and make-up days.
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.rationale: Of the 2,430 scheduled games, the share that remain after a given delay depends on how the schedule is spread (about 13 to 15 games per calendar day on average, with fewer on Mondays and in April) and on whether MLB prefers to compress by doubleheaders, cancel series or play 162 by extending the season. The 600-game strike corresponds to a very late start or season cancellation.

mlb.hitter_speed.measurement: Sprint speed (ft/s) = Statcast competitive-run sprint speed, season-to-date blended with the prior season by competitive runs with k = 15 runs, age-adjusted with the empirical yearly decline fitted on 2015-2025. Infield-hit rate = infield hits / ground balls in play, shrunk to league with k = 100 grounders; extra-base-taken rate = extra bases taken / opportunities, shrunk with k = 40 opportunities. Apply: BABIP shift = slope * (speed - league mean), with slope from a regression of BABIP on sprint speed controlling for exit velocity and launch angle (2021-2025); steal attempt covariate z = (speed - mean)/SD. Output speed index and BABIP and SB attempt shifts. As-of: through the previous day.
mlb.hitter_speed.mechanism: Faster runners beat out infield grounders, steal more bases and take extra bases, adding hits, runs and SB probability.
mlb.hitter_speed.rationale: Sprint speed adds a small increment to BABIP and drives steal and triple probability. Subtle: speed declines with age and injury, and attempts depend on manager.

mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.label: Home Run Derby round output under the 2026 swing-capped format: swings allotted, per-swing HR rate, last-swing extension and advancement
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.measurement: Per hitter: p = P(HR | swing) estimated from season barrel rate, pulled fly-ball rate and max-EV percentile (through the day before the Derby) mapped to Derby HR per swing using 2015-2025 Derby swing logs (timed-format years, swing outcomes only, not volume), shrunk to the pooled Derby mean with k = 40 swings, adjusted by the BP-pitcher term and host-park carry. Round HR ~ Binomial(n_r, p) + extension E where E is geometric with P(last swing HR) x p/(1-p) expected extra homers; n_r = 20, 15, 15. Fatigue as a multiplicative decay on p per round (prior 0.97, shrunk). Simulate the pool, the longest-HR Round 1 tiebreak and three-swing swing-offs. As-of: field and rulebook at the snapshot.
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.mechanism: With a fixed swing allotment (20 in Round 1, 15 in the semifinal and final) a round's homers equal the sum of per-swing HR indicators plus a geometric extension when the last allotted swing is a homer; the clock, pitcher pace and bonus time no longer exist.
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.rationale: Under swing caps volume is fixed, so the levers are per-swing HR rate, selectivity (takes appear not to count against the allotment, so waiting for a hittable pitch costs nothing but time) and the quality of the hitter's chosen batting-practice pitcher. Round 1 is an eight-man pool where the top four advance, so the advancement threshold depends on the whole field's rates, not on one opponent.

mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.label: Derby extremes: probability of 500+ foot homers, longest homer and peak exit velocity over the event

Number of draws per hitter = homers from the throughput model, i.e. 20 Round 1 swings, plus 15 more if he reaches the semifinal and 15 more in the final, plus extensions; this makes extremes depend on bracket advancement, not clock. Adjust for host-park carry from mlb.park_specific_xhr and weather. Simulate jointly with the throughput model because the Round 1 tie rule (longest HR) couples totals and distances; report P(any >= 525 ft), P(500+ count >= k), P(each hitter has longest), P(each hitter has highest EV HR). As-of: games through the previous day.

mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.rationale: A batter's average HR distance says little about whether he reaches 500 or 525 ft. Longest and highest-EV series are dead-heated at the league's reported precision, so rounding matters.

mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.label: Joint season HR-SB distribution for one hitter (power-speed profile, PA, availability)
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.measurement: Given current HR_0, SB_0, team games remaining G, per-game play probability from availability and PA per game by lineup slot, set rates r_HR and r_SB per PA = (ROS projection * 250 + season pace * n)/(250 + n) with n = season PA. Simulate 20,000 seasons: PA_rest from game draws with a health hazard; HR_rest ~ NegBin(mean r_HR*PA_rest, dispersion fitted across hitters 2015-2025) and SB_rest ~ NegBin(mean r_SB*PA_rest); couple the two with a Gaussian copula whose rho is the cross-hitter correlation of season HR and SB rate residuals given PA (2015-2025). Output P(HR_0 + HR_rest >= H* and SB_0 + SB_rest >= S*) for contract thresholds. As-of: daily.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.mechanism: A 50 HR and 40 SB season is a joint tail of two correlated counts requiring health and PA.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.rationale: The probability depends on the hitter's season-to-date pace, remaining PA and the rates of both events, and the two are correlated through playing time and hitter quality; independence misprices.

mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.label: Labour-stoppage regime: CBA expiry (Dec 1 2026), lockout flag and expected end, and transaction freeze rules

mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.mechanism: A lockout freezes 40-man roster transactions and free-agent signings, turning a window into a pre-expiry rush, a frozen interval of unknown length and a post-deal rush.
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.rationale: The 2022 CBA expires at 11:59 pm ET on Dec 1 2026 and a lockout is widely reported as likely; in 2021-22 the lockout froze 40-man transactions from Dec 2 until Mar 10 2022. A next-team market closing Mar 25 2027 and any call-up or opening-day contract in 2027 are therefore mixtures over stoppage length, and 15 years of calendar hazard history include only one such stoppage.

mlb.late_replacement_risk.label: Early-removal and pinch-hit-for risk for a starting hitter (PA truncation)
mlb.late_replacement_risk.measurement: For each hitter-season and k in {3, 4, 5}: a game is eligible if the team's PA count reached 9*(k-1) + slot (the hitter's slot would have its k-th PA). Event 'removed before PA k' = hitter has fewer than k PAs in an eligible game. Estimate P(removed before PA k) by the score state at his previous PA (lead >= 4, within 3, trail >= 4) and the opposing reliever hand, with hitter rates shrunk to role-class means (everyday, platoon, catcher, veteran DH) with k = 60 games. Output survival probabilities to PA3, PA4, PA5. As-of: confirmed lineup plus the model score-state distribution.
mlb.late_replacement_risk.mechanism: A starter may be lifted for a pinch hitter or defensive replacement, so PA count is truncated and the late PAs against the bullpen go to someone else.
mlb.late_replacement_risk.rationale: Slot-based PA expectations assume a full game; platoon players, catchers and aging regulars are routinely removed in high-leverage late innings or in blowouts, and the settlement counts only the starter's own PAs.

mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure.label: Lightning-proximity exposure within the league's 8-mile safety radius over the game window
mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure.measurement: Target: P(at least one lightning flash within 8 miles of the park from first pitch to first pitch + 3.5 hours). Historical frequency f(park, month, local hour) from GOES-R GLM flashes (2018 onward) within 8 miles of park coordinates. Forecast-conditioned probability from a logistic regression of the flash indicator on forecast CAPE and probability of thunder at the vintage 3 hours before first pitch, calibrated on 5 seasons of games and shrunk to f with k = 40 games per park-month. Separately calibrate P(delay | flash) against recorded weather delays. The 8-mile radius is a modelling convention, not a league rule; GLM optical flashes proxy NLDN strikes. As-of: 3 hours before first pitch and lineup post.
mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure.mechanism: Lightning within a set radius triggers mandatory delays independent of rain amount.
mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure.rationale: A forecast of rain probability misses thunderstorms with sparse precipitation; lightning radius rules cause delays even when the field is dry, and conversely rain can come without lightning and be played through.

mlb.lineup_strength_delta.label: Day-specific lineup strength delta (confirmed lineup vs team baseline, in runs per game)
mlb.lineup_strength_delta.measurement: delta (runs per game) = sum over slots s of PA_share(s) * (wOBA_proj(hitter_s vs starter hand) - wOBA_proj(baseline_s vs same hand)) / 1.2, where baseline_s = the hitter with the most starts at slot s over the team's last 30 games (PA-weighted if tied) and PA_share = (4.65, 4.55, 4.45, 4.35, 4.25, 4.15, 4.05, 3.95, 3.85), summing to 38.25 PA so no further multiplier is applied. wOBA_proj blends the average of the ZiPS and Steamer ROS projections with 2-season xwOBA shrunk to the projection with k = 300 PA, platoon-adjusted. Units: runs per game (0.100 team-wide wOBA is about 3.2 runs). As-of: lineup post with the projection vintage at that time.
mlb.lineup_strength_delta.mechanism: The nine hitters who actually play differ from the team's season baseline because of rest days, platoon choices and injuries.
mlb.lineup_strength_delta.rationale: Team-level wRC+ averages across the season's lineups; the confirmed card might lack its best hitter or contain a bench bat, and the effect is not uniform across the order (top slots get more PAs).

mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.label: Lockout and shortened-season scenario: P(lockout), start/end dates and games lost under each scenario
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.measurement: Scenario mixture: P(no lockout) from negotiation state (own timestamped coding of reports, ordinal 0-4); conditional on a lockout, the stoppage end date drawn from a survival model with prior from 1990, 1994-95 and 2021-22 (3 events, strongly shrunk) updated by negotiation stage; games lost = schedule games before the agreed start date after a compressed ramp-up (about 3 weeks of spring training), with doubleheaders making up part. Output: P(first regular-season game before May 31 2027) and P(games played > 600) = P(games lost < 1,830). As-of: daily.
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.mechanism: A CBA lockout after Dec 1 2026 could delay opening day and cancel games, so season-games and opening-day outcomes are mixtures over scenarios.
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.rationale: A 600-game strike equals roughly a quarter of the 2,430-game schedule and a May 31 opening cutoff is a long delay; both are plausible stoppage thresholds. In 2021-22 the lockout postponed opening day by about one week with no games lost (to my knowledge), but 1994-95 lost the end of one season and the start of the next; the distribution of games lost is heavy-tailed with a large mass at zero.

mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.label: Longest winning streak: extreme-value distribution given team win probabilities and remaining games
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.measurement: For team i with games remaining n_i, current streak c_i and per-game win prob p_ij: P(longest streak >= L) computed by a run-length Markov chain; account for heterogeneity of p_ij by opponent and home/away, and current maximum across league to date. P(team has strict maximum) = Prod over rivals (1 - ...) with Monte Carlo and tie share 1/N (payout rounded down). Streak serial correlation assumed zero unless tested. As-of: daily. Units: probability. Postponed, suspended and cancelled games are excluded from the sequence; the streak model assumes independent games conditional on p_ij, so serial correlation and doubleheader order are assumptions.
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.mechanism: The longest win streak across teams is the maximum over runs of consecutive wins; the season-level maximum is an extreme value.
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.rationale: Season streak markets are filed in this archetype but are not inning markets; the winning team is the one with the longest run, with ties paying $1/N, so the exact distribution of the maximum run for each team (given per-game win probability, mostly 0.4-0.65) determines the odds.

mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher.label: Ninth-inning entry state (score margin, home-bats flag) and expected pitcher and due-up slots
mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher.measurement: P(home bats bottom 9) = P(home not leading after top 9) from the run distribution after 8 innings and top-9 runs. Margin entering 9 from simulated score distribution (innings 1-8). Pitcher: P(closer) = P(save situation: lead 1-3 for the home team entering visitor's top? (visitors pitching vs home)); for the visitor's top 9 the pitcher is the home team's closer if home leads by <=3, otherwise a setup/mop-up arm. Closer availability from usage in prior 2 days (back-to-back/3-in-4 flags). Due-up slots from expected PAs through eight innings (0-8 batters). Output: expected runs in top-9 and bottom-9 and P(any run). As-of: lineup post (prior) and live updates. WALK-OFF STOPPING RULE: bottom-9 (and later) runs are computed from a half-inning chain that terminates when the home team takes the lead. Tied entering the bottom: P(any run) = P(chain reaches a go-ahead run), and the run count is 1 unless the final hit is a home run (then 1 + runners on). Home trailing by d: only the first d+1 runs can score, again with the homer exception. This truncated distribution, not the untruncated half-inning run distribution, feeds KXMLBINNINGTOTAL over 1.5 and the Tie strike of KXMLBINNINGWIN.
mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher.mechanism: The 9th inning's run distribution depends on whether the home team bats, the margin, and who pitches.
mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher.rationale: KXMLBINNINGTOTAL and KXMLBINNINGWIN settle on the ninth only, including the case where the home team skips the bottom. The probability that the bottom of the ninth is played falls with home-team lead probability, and the pitcher is the closer in save situations or a mop-up arm in blowouts.

Deviation from the average on a specific day (wind out to right) matters most for hitters who hit to that sector.

mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.label: Within-pitcher situational velocity lift: change in fastball speed with leverage, postseason, inning of appearance, pitch number, count, days of rest and temperature

Fit by REML on all regular and postseason pitches from the 4 seasons before the as-of date only. Output per-situation additive lift in mph with standard errors, added to a pitcher's baseline speed distribution location parameter (scale unchanged). Units: mph. As-of: refit each offseason, recomputed preseason; no data dated after the as-of used.

mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.rationale: Velocity rises in the postseason and in high-leverage spots, falls after consecutive days of work and with pitch count, and is expected to be lower in colder air (effect size unverified, see velo_temperature_effect). Because the threshold sits in the extreme tail, a lift of half a mph multiplies the exceedance probability many times.

mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.measurement: Role = SP if the pitcher started the last start, RP otherwise, opener if started and faced <=6 batters. Speed shift = within-pitcher difference in 99th percentile fastball speed between relief and starting appearances, estimated on pitchers with >=100 fastballs in each role, shrunk to the league mean shift with k = 15 pitchers' equivalents of 100 fastballs. mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.mechanism: Starters pace velocity over 90-100 pitches while one-inning relievers throw every pitch near peak, so the same arm reaches higher speeds in relief.
mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.rationale: A hard-throwing starter typically sits 1.5-3 mph above his starting average when used in short relief. mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.label: Playoff walk-off count: remaining-games exposure and per-game walk-off probability
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.measurement: Count so far W0 from official game results. Remaining games G are random: enumerate bracket paths and series lengths (best-of-5 or 7) from own per-game win probabilities. For each future game compute p_walkoff = P(home team trails by <=3 or is tied entering the bottom of the 9th and takes the lead before three outs, or wins in an extra inning) from the game run model plus half-inning chain with the visiting closer and due-up slots (walk-off stopping rule), shrunk to the league postseason rate over 2015-2025 with k = 100 games. P(count >= N) = P(W0 + sum Bernoulli(p_g) >= N) integrated over the distribution of G (Poisson-binomial mixture). Units: count and probability. As-of: daily during the playoffs.
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.mechanism: A walk-off is a home-team win in the bottom of the 9th or an extra inning; the playoff count is the sum over remaining playoff games of a Bernoulli event whose probability depends on late-inning state, closer quality and who is home.
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.rationale: KXMLBWALKOFFS pays on at least N walk-offs across the playoffs (the run that gives the home team the lead ends the game), so it is a count over a random number of games, with the count so far fixed. The per-game probability is not constant: it needs the home team to be tied or trailing by a small margin entering its last at-bat and to score the go-ahead run, and it varies with bullpen quality, extras probability and home-team identity.

mlb.scoreless_streak_survival.measurement: Define the streak in outs. For each future outing j compute, by dynamic programming over the 24 base-out states within each half-inning, the probability S_j(k) of recording k consecutive outs with no run charged to the pitcher (counting all runs, and separately earned runs only). Transition probabilities from the pitcher's projected K%, BB%, HR/PA and BABIP vs the opponent lineup and park, each shrunk to league with k = 300 batters faced. Outs per outing from mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve. P(reach N) = P(streak of N innings completed) summed over the outings remaining before season end by recursion on the carried streak. Add P(inherited runner scores) from bullpen strand rate. Units: probability. As-of: after each outing.
mlb.scoreless_streak_survival.mechanism: A scoreless streak extends by one third of an inning per out recorded without a run charged to the pitcher and ends at the first charged run, so reaching N is a survival product over the outs still needed.
mlb.scoreless_streak_survival.rationale: KXMLBSISTREAK settles on consecutive scoreless innings counted in thirds; elite starters post per-inning scoreless rates near 0.80, so a ten-inning gap has probability around 0.1 and is extremely sensitive to the per-inning rate, opponents, parks and whether runners he leaves on base later score. The contract does not say whether unearned runs break the streak, so both definitions must be computed.

mlb.series_game_dependence.rationale: Spread (sweep) and exact-score cells are tail cells of the score distribution, so a small positive correlation shifts them far more than it shifts the winner probability. The parameter must be estimated, not assumed zero, and its uncertainty carried.

mlb.series_per_game_win_prob_vector.label: Market-free per-game win probability for each remaining game of a series, built from starters, bullpen availability, lineup and home edge

mlb.series_per_game_win_prob_vector.mechanism: The series is a first-to-N path through game probabilities that differ by game because the starter, bullpen state and home team change; this input is the vector p_1..p_N those components produce.

mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.label: Starter removal hazard per batter faced (discrete-time survival curve)
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.measurement: Discrete-time logistic hazard h(b) = P(removed after batter b | still in) estimated on 5 seasons of starts (regular season; separate postseason intercept). Predictors: batters faced b (spline, knots at 9, 18, 27), pitch count (spline), runs allowed so far (0,1,2,3+), runners on at b, team lead/deficit bucket, days rest, season-to-date average pitches per start (shrunk to league with k = 8 starts), manager random effect (shrunk, k = 40 starts), bullpen-freshness index (relievers used last 2 days). Output: survival S(b) for b = 1..36 and E[BF]. As-of: manager and pitcher effects fit through the prior game; game-state predictors enter only inside a simulation, not as pregame data.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.mechanism: Batters faced is a first-passage time with removal hazard depending on pitch count, trip through the order, runs allowed and manager.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.rationale: The existing 'leash' label names the idea but gives no estimand. A K ladder cares about P(survive to batter 25+) and the hook is not a function of innings alone: a starter at 85 pitches with a 4-run deficit is removed at a different rate than one with a lead, and managers differ in whether they pull at the third-time-through boundary or at a pitch count. A measured hazard curve turns leash into a number the strikeout model can integrate over.

mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.label: Start-level dispersion of strikeouts beyond Poisson-binomial (rho parameter)
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.measurement: From 4 seasons of starts: for each start compute standardized residual of K given modelled expected K per batter faced (Pearson z = (K - sum p_i)/sqrt(sum p_i(1-p_i))). Estimate rho by moment matching: Var(K) = sum p_i(1-p_i) + rho*sum_{i!=j} sqrt(p_i(1-p_i)p_j(1-p_j)); pool pitchers by arsenal cluster (fastball-heavy, breaking-ball-heavy, finesse) and shrink to the pooled value with k = 25 starts. Report rho by cluster and by temperature bucket. As-of: estimated through the prior season, refreshed weekly in-season.
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.mechanism: Strikeouts across the nine batters share a pitcher-day latent state, so counts are more dispersed than independent Bernoulli draws.
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.rationale: The ladder prices neighbouring rungs from one distribution; if the variance is too small the 10+ and 11+ rungs are systematically underpriced and the 4+ rungs overpriced for high-K arms. A per-pitcher (or per-archetype) intra-start correlation parameter is the cheapest way to calibrate the width.

mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.label: Two-strike putaway decomposition: P(reach 2 strikes) x P(K | 2 strikes) by batter hand
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.measurement: For each pitcher, 3 seasons of pitch-level data with half-life 120 batters faced: r2 = share of PAs that reach 2 strikes (by batter hand); c2 = K / PAs reaching 2 strikes. For each batter: his own r2_b and c2_b, shrunk to league-by-hand with k = 150 PAs for r2 and k = 120 two-strike PAs for c2. Combine with odds-ratio (log5) per sub-event: logit(r2_match) = logit(r2_p) + logit(r2_b) - logit(r2_league), same for c2; matchup P(K) = r2_match * c2_match. Sum over the confirmed order weighted by expected PA per slot. Units: probability per PA; as-of the lineup-post timestamp using only games dated before the game.
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.mechanism: A strikeout needs two sub-events: the PA reaches a two-strike count, then the pitcher converts. The two pieces are driven by different pitches (first-pitch and early-count strikes versus chase/whiff pitches).
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.rationale: Aggregate K% and CSW hide that a pitcher can have a high K% from elite putaway on few two-strike PAs (fragile to lineup contact skill) or from reaching two strikes constantly (stable). Opposing hitters differ separately on 'gets to two strikes' (takes, fouls) and 'strikes out once there' (whiff on the chase pitch), so the matchup must be applied to each sub-event, not to the end rate.

mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.rationale: A single rating hides that April uncertainty is large and that roster shocks widen it; futures prices at tails (95+ wins, a long-shot pennant) depend on the variance more than the mean.

mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution.label: P(extra innings) from the inning-by-inning score chain, including tie-restoring bottom-9 halves
mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution.measurement: P(extras) = sum over states s of P(state s entering bottom 9) x P(home half-inning ends with score level), computed from an inning-by-inning Markov chain: states are (run differential after top 9, outs=0) with visitor closer PA rates (shrunk to league reliever rates, k = 150 BF) and home due-up hitters. Tied entering bottom 9: P(level) = P(home scores 0). Home trailing by d>=1: P(level) = P(home scores exactly d runs without taking the lead, the half ends on the third out). Home leading: no bottom 9, P(extras)=0. Walk-off stopping rule applied, so the half-inning ends once the home team takes the lead. Validate on 5 seasons by comparing predicted and observed extras rate by pre-game expected-total decile. Units: probability. As-of: confirmed lineups.
mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution.mechanism: Extras occur whenever the score is level after nine complete innings (or after the home half is played to its end), so the event is a function of the joint inning-by-inning chain, not of a single tied-entering-the-ninth conditional.
mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution.rationale: KXMLBEXTRAS pays when at least one extra inning is played. Games reach extras by two routes: tied after the top of the 9th with the home team failing to score, and visitors leading after the top of the 9th with the home team tying the score but not taking the lead (the half-inning ends on the third out, not on the tying run). Modelling only the first route understates P(extras); the home walk-off stopping rule also truncates the bottom-9 run distribution.

mlb.weather_pit.rationale: Hot/humid conditions and out-blowing wind raise run scoring; cold and in-blowing wind lower it. Subtle: forecasts update through the day and the realised first-pitch weather differs, wind relative to field orientation matters (need park azimuth), and roofed/dome parks are excluded or conditional on roof state.

mlb.wind_vector_park.label: Wind vector relative to park orientation and roof state
mlb.wind_vector_park.measurement: Compute wind component = speed x cos(wind direction - park home-plate-to-centre bearing); HR/total multiplier from historical regression; roof status flag from team announcements.
mlb.wind_vector_park.mechanism: Wind blowing out or in along the field axis and the roof state change fly-ball carry and thus HR and total runs.
mlb.wind_vector_park.rationale: Raw wind direction (compass) is useless without park azimuth; in/out components and crosswinds differ by park geometry. Subtle: forecast error is larger for wind than temperature, and retractable roofs are decided close to first pitch.

mlb.window_exposure_schedule.label: Window exposure: games, off days, doubleheaders and role-probability per game within the window
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.measurement: N = number of team games in the window from the official schedule (adjust for postponement probability from mlb.forecast_precip_timing). Per-game participation p_g: hitters from mlb.playing_time_role start probability, pitchers from mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest P(start on date) plus relief-appearance rate for relievers. P(healthy through g) = (1 - h)^g with per-game injury hazard h from mlb.injuries_pit shrunk to league by age/role (k = 100 player-seasons). P(at least one) = 1 - prod_g (1 - p_g x P(healthy through g)); multiply by (1 - clinched rest factor) from mlb.clinched_rest_policy after the clinch date. Units: probability. As-of: daily.
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.mechanism: A multi-game window aggregates per-game participation probabilities with schedule structure.
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.rationale: P(at least one) in a window depends on the number of team games remaining (off days, doubleheaders, postponement) and on the team's usage pattern; a two-way player's pitching is limited by rotation turns.

mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.label: Season state: wins, losses, games remaining, run differential to date and ties/suspended games
mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.measurement: Daily from standings: W, L, G_rem = 162 - W - L (adjusted for suspended or cancelled games per the official schedule), W_needed = N - W, run differential RD and pythagenpat win% to date. P(wins >= N) = sum over k >= W_needed of P(Bin-mixture(G_rem, p_i)) where p_i is the per-game probability from the talent posterior. Units: wins and games. As-of: after each day's final games.
mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.mechanism: A win-total threshold is wins already banked plus the number of wins in the remaining games, so the state variables set how much uncertainty is left.
mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.rationale: The primary state of a win-total ladder is not a rating but how many wins are banked and how many games remain; the required additional wins W_needed = N - wins and the remaining games determine the binomial tail, and the posterior from run differential only prices the per-game probability. Suspended or cancelled games change games remaining.

mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour.label: Crew-specific word and phrase rate per broadcast hour with dispersion (transcript-based)
mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour.measurement: From transcripts (ASR with timestamps) of 40+ games per crew: for each word w count n_gw and exposure hours t_g; fit negative-binomial n_gw ~ NB(mean = t_g * lambda_cw, dispersion phi_cw) with lambda_cw shrunk to national lexeme rate with k = 6 games and phi pooled by word class. Stemming rules follow the contract text version. P(at least one) = 1 - integrated NB zero probability given expected exposure. As-of: before first pitch with crew known.
mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour.mechanism: Each crew has a characteristic per-hour rate for each lexeme and a dispersion beyond Poisson.
mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour.rationale: The catalog's mention_text names crew language tendencies without a measurement; the question needs per-word per-crew rates and a dispersion estimate because probability of at least one is concave in the rate and depends on clustering.

Under a fixed swing allotment the chosen pitcher's speed and location consistency scale the hitter's per-swing HR probability; the gain compounds through the last-swing extension, so a good pairing helps high-rate hitters more than low-rate ones.

all_star_week_events.label: All-Star Game and Home Run Derby events
all_star_week_events.mechanism: All three events are exhibitions generated by who participates and how they are used, not by season-long roles. In the All-Star Game, selection and withdrawal define the pool, managers rotate starters, reserves and one-inning pitchers, and a tie after nine innings goes to a swing-off whose statistics do not count for player props; the MVP is a panel and fan choice. The Futures Game is a seven-inning prospect exhibition priced from translated minor-league talent. In the 2026 Derby, an eight-player field takes 20 swings in a Round 1 pool and 15 in the semifinal and final, so homers are per-swing HR rate times a fixed allotment plus last-swing extensions, and longest-homer, 500+ ft and exit-velocity series are tail extremes over a draw count set by rounds reached.
all_star_week_events.target: Result or player/event stat in the All-Star Game, the Futures Game or the Home Run Derby (winner, MVP, player hits/HR/strikeouts, total HR, Derby selection, advancement, round totals, longest HR, distance and exit-velocity extremes).

interactions.hypothesis: A prospect's exact-slot chance depends on whether the club at that slot historically prefers his profile, so the same board rank gives different slot odds under different orders.
Insider links carry most information when boards disagree; when boards agree tightly, reports add little beyond the consensus rank.
Clubs pursuing underslot deals favour low-leverage college seniors, so high-demand prep players slide further at slots held by pool-constrained clubs.
A medical or bonus-demand flag moves a top-three prospect little but pushes a prospect ranked 6-12 out of the top 10, so the slide depends on consensus rank.

The probability that a prospect goes at slot k is conditional on which club holds k: a club that takes college bats almost exclusively raises a college hitter's slot-k chance and lowers a prep pitcher's, independently of board rank.

When boards agree (rank SD below about 2) the consensus rank predicts the slot well and insider links add little; when boards disagree, the selection is decided by club-specific links and reports dominate.

A high bonus demand only causes a slide at slots held by clubs planning underslot deals; at slots held by clubs paying full slot it costs little, so slide risk is demand times the club's underslot propensity.

A medical or demand flag moves a prospect differently by rank: a top-three player with a flag still goes inside the top 10, while a player ranked 6-12 with the same flag slides out of it, because no club at the top needs to take the risk.
A club-player link moves probability in proportion to the reporting writer's historical exact-slot hit rate; a link from a low-accuracy mock is close to noise.

amateur_draft_selection.label: MLB Draft pick position markets
amateur_draft_selection.mechanism: The MLB Draft is a sequential without-replacement selection. The order of clubs at slots 1-10 is fixed by the lottery (picks 1-6), reverse prior-season record, luxury-tax pick moves and inserted compensation picks, and first-round picks cannot be traded. Each club then takes the highest player on its own board after adjusting for its bonus pool strategy, its front-office tendency and each prospect's medicals and signability; many top picks are pre-agreed below slot. A prospect's slot is therefore the outcome of consensus talent rank, club-specific deviation and the cascade of choices ahead of him.
amateur_draft_selection.target: Whether a named prospect is selected at an exact overall pick or within the top N picks of the MLB Draft.

labour_stoppage_and_season_schedule.mechanism: The outcome is produced by owner-union collective bargaining after the CBA expires on December 1, 2026, not by games. interactions.hypothesis: Exceedance requires both a near-threshold ceiling and many attempts; volume without ceiling contributes almost nothing, so the two multiply inside the tail.
Postseason bullpen use of hard-throwing starters converts paced pitches into max-effort pitches, concentrating record chances in October.
The situational lift (temperature included as a fixed effect) shifts the per-pitch mean, and at a threshold beyond the record a small additive lift multiplies the tail probability.
A falling velocity trend signals elevated injury hazard, so exposure loss and lower ceiling arrive together rather than independently.

Season exceedance is roughly 1 - exp(-N x p): N near-peak pitches times the per-pitch tail p given the ceiling. A pitcher topping out 3 mph below the line has p near zero, so even thousands of pitches add nothing; exposure only matters for arms whose ceiling is close.

A starter moved to the October bullpen switches from paced effort to max effort, raising his top-speed distribution by one to three mph for the remaining appearances; regular-season starter exposure says little about this regime.

An additive lift (leverage, rest, temperature, all fixed effects inside the lift input) shifts the per-pitch distribution, and because the threshold sits in the bounded tail, tail probability rises convexly with the lift until close to the endpoint.

Velocity decline and injury tend to arrive together, so a falling trend lowers both the ceiling and the expected remaining exposure; treating them as independent overstates the probability for declining candidates.

Park speed offsets bias a candidate's measured ceiling depending on where he pitches; a closer whose home park reads hot appears closer to the threshold, and the contract settles on that biased reading.

When the best candidate ceilings sit more than about 2 mph under the line the physical exceedance probability is near zero and the anomaly rate sets P(YES); only when a candidate's ceiling approaches the line does the physical tail dominate, so the weight on each route switches with the ceiling gap.

pitch_velocity_extremes.label: Season maximum pitch velocity thresholds (player or league-wide)
pitch_velocity_extremes.mechanism: The season's fastest pitch is the maximum of a bounded per-pitch speed distribution taken over a few thousand near-peak fastballs from a small pool of elite throwers. Exceeding a threshold beyond the tracked record needs a pitcher whose ceiling sits close to it, enough max-effort attempts (relief use, postseason), favourable situations (rest, warmth, leverage), continued health and a tracking reading that lands above the line. The tail is bounded by physiology, so exceedance probabilities beyond the observed record fall off faster than an exponential tail would imply.
pitch_velocity_extremes.target: Whether a named pitcher, or any pitcher, throws a pitch at or above a velocity threshold (e.g. 107 MPH) in any game of the season including playoffs, per tracked pitch speed.

Walk-offs need games, and only games that reach the home team's last at-bat tied or narrowly behind; the count is therefore games remaining (set by bracket path and series length) times a per-game rate that rises with evenly matched, low-scoring pairings. A long series between two strong pitching staffs raises both factors at once, so the two cannot be estimated separately.

The playoff HR total is a compound sum: its variance is the variance of the number of games times the squared per-game mean plus the per-game dispersion times the expected games. Early in October the games-remaining term dominates and the threshold probability moves in steps with each series result; late, per-game park and weather matter more.

A 2+ series home-run rung needs two events, so its probability rises faster than linearly in total plate appearances: a series that goes seven games instead of four nearly doubles a hitter's chances for 1+ but more than triples them for 2+, and the effect is larger for high per-PA power rates.

In the date-window market a healthy power hitter's probability saturates quickly (he usually homers within a few weeks), so almost all uncertainty is the injury state: a hitter on the injured list with an uncertain return has a probability governed by return timing, not power.

A streak can only reach N if enough starts remain to record the needed outs: late in the season the rung becomes impossible once remaining starts times outs per start falls below the gap, regardless of how dominant the pitcher is.

Runners a streaking pitcher leaves on base and who later score are charged to him and, if the streak counts all charged runs, break it; managers protecting a streak pull him with bases empty, so the bullpen and exit-state policy change survival late in starts.

playoff_series_markets.label: Playoff series winner, total games, spread and games hosted
playoff_series_markets.mechanism: A series is a first-to-N path through per-game win probabilities that differ by game: the bracket sets the home pattern, off days and rainouts move the rotation so each game has a different starter, bullpen fatigue accumulates (worse after extra innings, which have no automatic runner in the postseason) and resets, and rosters change between rounds. Winner, total games, spread and exact score are functions of the same series score; games hosted is seed probability times rounds reached times the home pattern, so before the bracket is set it is driven by regular-season seeding.
playoff_series_markets.target: Winner, number of games, game margin of a best-of-N postseason series, or number of playoff games a club hosts.
